related_questions.question: Do I need the new COVID booster?

text_blocks.snippet: Whether or not to get the latest COVID-19 booster depends on individual circumstances. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends the updated vaccine for those who are unvaccinated, those 65 and older, those at high risk for severe illness, those in long-term care, and pregnant individuals. The CDC also states that even those who have already had COVID-19 should still get the updated vaccine.

list.title: Age and underlying health conditions:
list.snippet: Individuals 65 and older and those with underlying health conditions are more vulnerable to severe illness from COVID-19 and should prioritize getting the booster.

list.title: Pregnancy:
list.snippet: Pregnant individuals should get the updated vaccine to protect themselves and their infants.

list.title: Risk of exposure:
list.snippet: If you have a high risk of exposure to COVID-19, due to your job or social circumstances, the updated vaccine is a good idea.

list.title: Individual risk assessment:

related_questions.question: What are the side effects of the 5th COVID booster?
related_questions.snippet: Common side effects include pain at the injection site, fever, body aches and headaches. These reactions are frequent (and indicate that your body is making an immune response to the vaccine) and should go away within 1-2 days, with the exception that swollen lymph nodes may persist up to about 10 days.

related_questions.question: What vaccines need boosters as adults?

text_blocks.snippet: Several vaccines require booster shots for adults. The Tdap vaccine (tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis) is recommended for all adults, with a booster shot every 10 years. Additionally, pregnant women should receive the Tdap vaccine during each pregnancy to protect the newborn. Other vaccines like influenza (flu) and COVID-19 also have recommendations for regular boosters. Furthermore, adults over 50 should consider a booster for shingles, and those at risk may need boosters for other vaccines like hepatitis A or B.

list.title: Shingles:
